catalog_quote: [Singh 2003, ch. II, 2.0] In Purum language there are three major sound systems. They are vowels, consonants and tone. These sound systems consist of six vowels phonemes, nineteen consonant phonemes and two tones. ... [2.4 TONE, printed p. 39] In Purum, there are two tones. They are falling and rising tones. The falling tone is marked (\) and rising tone is unmarked. Example 83. kə̀y “I” kəy “to pull” 84. mətʰòk “to encourage’ mətʰok “to drive” 85. sìn “small” sin “work” 86. wòk “pig” wok “to hit” 87. bòl “to make” bol “to bath” 88. ə̀wày “wide” əway “to feed” ... audit.reasoning: The coding (tonal; no word-stress rule stated; domain UNSTATED) rests on the language's Glottolog MED, a 246-pp descriptive grammar (PhD thesis 2003) whose entire phonology chapter we hold as a scan; the tone section was re-read today from the page image (printed p. 39) and matches the record verbatim, diacritics included; the thesis contents show no stress/accent section and the chapter scanned never mentions stress. Two independent supports are also verbatim in held files (Tezpur 2021 editors: two lexical tones; LSI 1904: stress placement unknown). The only better-dated source, Meitei 2021 (22-pp phonology chapter), is print-only (re-verified: the CFEL PDF is still 12 pp of front matter) and its editors' summary agrees with our coding, so nothing suggests a recode.
